rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Humans are primates among primates: Animalia, Chordata, Mammalia, order Primates, family Hominidae, species Homo sapiens. Our line left the apes through a sequence of fossils: Dryopithecus, the Miocene ape ancestor; Ramapithecus with heavy hominid jaws; Australopithecus — Lucy — walking upright with a small brain; Homo habilis with the first stone tools; Homo erectus taming fire; Neanderthals burying their dead with…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Taxonomic position: Animalia > Chordata > Mammalia > Primates > Hominidae > Homo > Homo sapiens
Evolutionary sequence: Australopithecus → H. habilis → H. erectus → H. neanderthalensis → H. sapiens
Key adaptations: bipedalism, encephalisation, language, culture

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Hominid vs hominin:** hominid = the great-ape family (gorillas, chimp, humans); hominin = humans and our ancestors after splitting from chimp lineage.  ·  **Australopithecus vs Homo:** Australopithecus walked upright but had ape-sized brains and made no stone tools; Homo shows larger brain + tools.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the taxonomic position of humans and a clear evolutionary sequence.  ·  Differentiate New World vs Old World monkeys and apes from monkeys (tail).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Lucy (A. afarensis, 3.2 mya)*** — the famous bipedal skeleton proving walking came before big brains.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Brain-hand-tool feedback loop:** bipedalism freed hands; tools rewarded intelligence; culture rewarded bigger brains — each pressure amplified the others.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Position: Animalia → Chordata → Mammalia → Primates → Hominidae → Homo sapiens.  ·  Stages: Dryopithecus (20–14 mya ape ancestor) → Ramapithecus (14–10 mya) → Australopithecus (4–1 mya, first biped, Lucy) → Homo habilis (tools, 650–750 cc) → Homo erectus (fire, 900–1100 cc) → Neanderthal (burial, ~1400 cc) → Homo sapiens (~1400 cc, culture).  ·  Trends: bipedalism → free hands → tools → brain → language → cultural evolution.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Modern humans and Neanderthals interbred — most non-African humans carry 1–2% Neanderthal DNA.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Where Do We Sit in the Tree of Life? Humans are animals — mammals, primates — distinguished not by separate creation but by a few decisive evolutionary acquisitions: upright walking, free hands, a large brain, language and culture. This topic places *Homo sapiens* in the animal kingdom and traces the hominid line from ape ancestors.  ·  ## 2. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Bipedalism BEFORE encephalisation is a key exam point.  ·  Neanderthals were NOT "primitive"; they had large brains and made tools.  ·  The 2024 stages question is compact — one line per stage with time and one feature is enough for 3 marks.

rows.label: More ideas
